findings.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 — RCE + Flag Extraction
findings.description: The /total_loan_payments endpoint builds its JSON response by rendering user-supplied GET parameters directly inside a Jinja2 template without sanitization. The `principal` parameter is injected into the template context, allowing an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary Jinja2 expressions and achieve full Remote Code Execution (RCE) as www-data on the underlying server. The CTF flag was extracted from /flag on the filesystem.

findings.title: Hardcoded Test Credentials in HTML Comment
findings.description: The login page HTML source contains a developer comment disclosing valid credentials: <!-- TODO: Delete the testing account (test:test). -->. This provides unauthenticated access to the application and was the initial access vector used before exploiting SSTI.
findings.evidence:
HTML comment: <!-- TODO: Delete the testing account (test:test). -->
Successful login: POST /login with username=test&password=test → 302 redirect to /home with valid session cookie
